Report_ID: Quality of life / psychological general well-being (PGWB total score) at 8 wk
Title: Ethyl-eicosapentaenoic acid for the treatment of psychological distress and depressive symptoms in middle-aged women: a double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized clinical trial
Author: Lucas M, Asselin G, Mérette C, Poulin MJ, Dodin S
Comment: Means/SDs are unadjusted week-8 values (n at week 8: E-EPA 55, placebo 51); the P value 0.2908 comes from the ANCOVA-adjusted 8-wk change difference (3.3; 95% CI: −2.9, 9.6), not from a test of the week-8 means. Higher PGWB = better well-being (no sign reversal needed). M_diff not recorded because the reported between-group difference is from a covariate-adjusted change analysis.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('E-EPA n-3 supplementation (1.05 g E-EPA/d + 0.15 g ethyl-DHA/d)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Study Environment: clinical (Centre Ménopause Québec, Saint-François d'Assise Hospital)
Participant type: middle-aged women (40–55 y) with moderate-to-severe psychological distress during menopausal transition; 24% met DSM-IV MDE criteria
Recruitment source: general population via newspaper, radio, television advertising and clinic flyers, Quebec, Canada
Outcome measurement: Unadjusted mean ± SD of PGWB total score at week 8, all randomized women
Outcome variable: Quality of life / psychological general well-being (PGWB total score) at 8 wk
effect_direction: favours omega-3 (PGWB total 68.3 vs 63.8), not statistically significant

Report_ID: SF-36 physical function score (physical component summary) at 8 weeks
Title: Effect of Omega-3 Fatty Acids Supplementation on Depressive Symptoms and on Health-Related Quality of Life in the Treatment of Elderly Women with Depression: A Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Randomized Clinical Trial
Author: Rondanelli et al.
Comment: p reported as "<0.001"; recorded as 0.001. M_diff is the paper's own unadjusted difference (21.1); SE_diff derived from its reported 95% CI as (31.4-10.8)/3.92 = 5.26. Scale range 0-100 stated in Methods ("The 8 scales were scored from 0 to 100 (worst to best possible health status)"). Higher score = better QoL.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('n-3 group (2.5 g/d n-3 LCPUFA: 1.67 g EPA + 0.83 g DHA)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Institutionalised depressed elderly women (aged 66-95 y) meeting DSM-IV-TR criteria for major depression or dysthymia
Outcome variable: SF-36 physical function score (physical component summary) at 8 weeks

Report_ID: KCCQ-TSS (heart failure-specific quality of life) at 12 weeks
Title: Long-Chain Omega-3 Fatty Acid Supplements in Depressed Heart Failure Patients: Results of the OCEAN Trial
Author: Jiang et al.
Comment: Table 2 values are adjusted means with STANDARD ERRORS in parentheses (recorded in _se fields, not _sd). Placebo n=28 is shared with the high-EPA arm row and must be split downstream.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('2:1 EPA/DHA (400/200 EPA/DHA, 2 g/day)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); ANOVA: missing F-value or group sizes
Design Type: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled parallel-group pilot trial
domain: cardiology / psychiatry (depression in chronic heart failure)
Study Environment: multicenter outpatient clinics (Duke, Thomas Jefferson, UNC Chapel Hill)
Participant type: Adults with chronic heart failure (NYHA >= II) and major depressive disorder (HAM-D >= 18)
Outcome measurement: Adjusted (least-squares) mean with standard error at endpoint
Outcome variable: KCCQ-TSS (heart failure-specific quality of life) at 12 weeks
additional_group_ns: High EPA arm not used in this row: n=23, KCCQ-TSS 58.1 (SE 2.7), p=0.94 vs placebo (extracted as a separate row)

Report_ID: Global Assessment of Functioning Scale score at 6 weeks (final)
Title: A Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study of the Omega-3 Fatty Acid Docosahexaenoic Acid in the Treatment of Major Depression
Author: Marangell et al.
Comment: GAF is a clinician-rated global functioning measure, not a patient-reported quality-of-life instrument; used as the closest available proxy. M_diff computed as placebo mean minus DHA mean (58.6 - 64.3) from the two explicitly reported group means in a simple two-group between-subjects comparison. No instrument scale range stated in the paper, so scale min/max left empty.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('DHA 2 g/day') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: adult outpatients (18-65) with DSM-IV nonpsychotic major depressive disorder
Recruitment source: outpatient clinical setting (institutional review board-approved site)
Outcome measurement: Mean final GAF score per group at study endpoint (6 weeks), with SD and two-sample t test
Outcome variable: Global Assessment of Functioning Scale score at 6 weeks (final)

Report_ID: Quality of life (Q-LES-Q % of max possible), change from baseline to week 8 — EPA-enriched n-3 vs placebo
Title: A Double-Blind, Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial Comparing Eicosapentaenoic Acid Versus Docosahexaenoic Acid for Depression
Author: Mischoulon et al.
Comment: Values are LS MEAN CHANGE scores with standard ERRORS (SE), not end-of-treatment means with SDs; SE recorded in the _se fields. F/df/P are for the overall 3-group treatment-by-time interaction, not the pairwise EPA-vs-placebo contrast. Placebo arm shared with the DHA arm (multi-arm trial): placebo n should be split downstream.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('EPA-enriched n-3 1,000 mg/d') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); treatment SD derived from its reported SE (SD = SE * sqrt(n)); control SD derived from its reported SE (SD = SE * sqrt(n)); N-DF MISMATCH (ANOVA): df1(2) + df2(733) + 1 = 736 ≠ n_total(177) — verify total sample size; N-INCONSISTENCY (multi-group): sum of additional_group_ns = 57 ≠ n_total(177) — verify all group Ns
Participant type: adult outpatients (ages 18-80) with DSM-IV major depressive disorder, baseline HDRS-17 >= 15
Recruitment source: Massachusetts General Hospital and Cedars-Sinai Medical Center outpatient clinics, advertisements and referrals
Outcome measurement: LS mean change from baseline (positive = improvement in quality of life)
Outcome variable: Quality of life (Q-LES-Q % of max possible), change from baseline to week 8 — EPA-enriched n-3 vs placebo
additional_group_ns: DHA-enriched n-3 arm (not used in this row): n = 57, LS mean change +10.89 (SE 1.39)
effect_direction: no meaningful difference (+11.05 vs +11.13; standardized effect −0.007, p=0.99)
